description: Multi-tenant sports-academy SaaS: static vanilla-JS tenant apps (LeoTennis, Machaxi, MatchPoint, MatchPoint Pride, Raj Sports) plus a native Android client and operator consoles (Academy Manager, CourtSync), all backed by one shared Supabase project (Postgres + RLS + Auth + Edge Function scaffolds). Gen Alpha is a federated tenant: it keeps its own Supabase project and reports telemetry rollups into the shared events table. THE HOUSE RULE: anything that computes money lives in Postgres — the fee chain, renewal roll-forward and payout split are SQL functions called by every client; no client does that arithmetic itself.

repos.AcademyManager: operator console (index.html single page) + platform schema/migrations/runner
repos.LeoTennis: tenant app template + supabase/ platform SQL (schema.sql, lockdown.sql, launch-reset.sql, edge functions)
repos.Machaxi: second tenant app, cloned from LeoTennis (two-venue model)
repos.MatchPoint: tenant app for Match Point Badminton Academy (Manikonda, Hyderabad); MatchPointBadminton repo is the superseded prototype
repos.MatchPointPride: separate app for the Pride venue owner (tenant 'mpp') — React 18 + TypeScript + Vite, the only React app on the platform; client-side money math removed in favor of the shared SQL functions
repos.Raj Sports: web console for coach-operator Raj (5 centres, 5 sports, NO bookings) + its own migration/cron SQL (fee chain, WhatsApp reminder engine)
repos.RajSportsApp: native Android client (Kotlin) for Raj Sports — same Supabase backend; breaking RPC changes ship as _v2
repos.genalpha-glass-web: Gen Alpha Cricket Academy glass web app — federated: runs on its own Supabase project and posts telemetry rollups to the shared events table; legacy repo cricket-academy-manager still serves genalphaacademy.in
repos.CourtSync: optional booking module + operator's cross-venue channel-sync board (on where tenants.config.modules.booking is true)

step_kinds.ui: a person acting in an app
step_kinds.failure: the failure path, or a known limitation

nodes.label: Players & Parents
nodes.desc: Public users: book courts, submit admission enquiries, pay fees.

nodes.label: Academy Staff
nodes.desc: Coaches/managers of one academy. Supabase Auth users with app_metadata {am_role:'staff', tenant_id}.

nodes.label: Platform Operator
nodes.desc: Runs the SaaS. Auth user with app_metadata {am_role:'operator'}; reads all tenants, aggregates only.

nodes.label: LeoTennis app
nodes.desc: Tenant 'leo'. Public pages (booking, admission, pay) + staff console (dashboard, bookings, players, fees, attendance). window.LT_CLOUD fetch adapter; fail-soft offline outbox.

nodes.label: Machaxi app
nodes.desc: Tenant 'machaxi'. Cloned from Leo; the sport dimension doubles as the venue court-pool key (rally R1-R6, urban U1-U7). Shares the github.io origin with Leo (mx-* storage keys).

nodes.label: MatchPoint app
nodes.desc: Tenant 'matchpoint'. Staff manager for Match Point Badminton Academy (Manikonda): attendance, bookings, fees, renewals — plus a full player-progress module.

nodes.label: MatchPoint Pride app
nodes.desc: Tenant 'mpp'. Separate app for the Pride venue owner (7 indoor courts, Narsingi) — the only React app on the platform. Its client-side money math was deleted (242 lines of selectors: unpaidMonthsFor, planFeeReminders, applyFeePlan) in favor of the same SQL functions every other client calls: resolve_fee, apply_payment_coverage, reminder_queue, record_fee_payment. Offline writes queue through an outbox that replays RPCs.

nodes.label: Raj Sports web
nodes.desc: Tenant 'raj'. Coaching manager for a coach-operator running batches at venues he doesn't own — centres can take revenue share. NO bookings module. Product priority: WhatsApp reminders that never give a parent a bad experience.

nodes.label: Raj Sports Android
nodes.desc: Native Android client for Raj Sports — same backend: signs in via Auth, reads ~14 tables over PostgREST, and calls 14 RPCs including the full money suite. Breaking RPC changes ship as _v2 — the app cannot be force-updated.

nodes.label: Gen Alpha app
nodes.desc: Gen Alpha Cricket Academy — the platform's FIRST client, live with real families. FEDERATED tenant (tenants.config.federated = true): keeps its own Supabase project and 19-table schema, and reports telemetry into the shared events table instead of migrating.

nodes.label: Academy Manager
nodes.desc: Portfolio KPIs, per-academy detail with a live 7-day activity feed, billing (set_subscription — audited in sync_log), growth, platform health. Account-level only: members and phone numbers never appear here.

nodes.label: CourtSync
nodes.desc: Operator's live channel-sync board across venues. Sold as an optional module — on only where tenants.config.modules.booking is true.

nodes.label: Supabase Auth
nodes.desc: Password sign-in for staff + operator; anon key for public paths. auth_role()/auth_tenant() helpers drive every RLS policy.

nodes.label: PostgREST API
nodes.desc: Direct table access gated by RLS: public may INSERT events + applications only; staff scoped to their tenant; operator reads everything.

nodes.label: SQL RPCs
nodes.desc: THE HOUSE RULE lives here: resolve_fee (7-level chain), record_fee_payment (the one write path), apply_payment_coverage, compute_payouts, reminder_queue, void/confirm_payment — plus request/record/confirm/cancel_booking, propagate_block/unblock, sync_ingest, submit_application, operator_portfolio, platform_health, reconcile_report. Public-by-design set is exactly: request_booking, submit_application, tenant_exists, tenant_publishes_timetable.

nodes.label: Postgres tables
nodes.desc: tenants, subscriptions, integrations, bookings, members, enrollments, fee_rules, payments, expenses, attendance, member_timeline, reminder_events, reminders_log, applications, events, sync_jobs, schema_migrations, platform_settings. Every row carries tenant_id; new tables are generic, per-tenant behaviour goes in tenants.config jsonb.

nodes.label: Derived views
nodes.desc: contacts (CRM deduped from bookings — read-only, can never break a booking) and public_slots (anon court availability, per-tenant opt-in via config.features.publicSlots).

nodes.label: sync_jobs queue
nodes.desc: Outbound cross-channel work enqueued transactionally, claimed with retry/backoff by process_sync_jobs every minute under pg_cron. Failures land in dead letters surfaced by platform_health.

nodes.label: pg_cron
nodes.desc: Every minute: process_sync_jobs drains the queue. Hourly: cron_health_check runs rls_audit/rpc_audit/policy_fn_audit + anon_probe + events_flowing. Nightly: reconcile + backup.take_snapshot (14-day retention, same database — free plan has no PITR).

nodes.label: Vault secrets
nodes.desc: Per-account partner credentials (partner:* secrets) set by staff via set_integration_secret, referenced from integrations.config — never plaintext, never in a client.

nodes.label: Edge Functions
nodes.desc: sync-worker, partner-webhook, partner-poll, partner-push, reconcile. Scaffolded, not yet deployed — the DB processor under pg_cron does the work meanwhile.

nodes.label: Partner channels
nodes.desc: Marketplace booking channels. Imports carry ext_ref; blocks propagate out so a slot sold anywhere closes everywhere. Inbound sync_ingest is authenticated by tenants.api_key.

nodes.label: WhatsApp
nodes.desc: Fee-renewal reminders with UPI pay links. Leo/Machaxi send from the staff roster (reminders_log); Raj runs the full ladder engine (reminder_events state machine, ported from Gen Alpha).

nodes.label: Gen Alpha Supabase
nodes.desc: Gen Alpha's own backend — its operational data (real families) stays here by design. Merging would mean migrating live data and rewriting a working app for nothing its owner would see.

edges.label: money · admin RPCs, 14 verified (_v2 on breaking changes)
federated telemetry: page_view · client_error · daily tenant_rollup (anon key)
fee chain · reminder RPCs (resolve_fee · record_fee_payment · reminder_queue · void_payment · reenroll_member)

flows.name: Player books a court
flows.summary: Public slot booking: server-side pricing, anti-abuse guards, atomic court claim, cross-channel blocking.

steps.title: Pick a slot
steps.detail: booking.html, no login. Availability comes from the anon-safe public_slots view — no PII crosses the wire.

steps.title: Anti-abuse gate
steps.detail: Anon RPC, verified guards: 6:00-22:00 only, <=90 days ahead, real 10-digit phone required, stale pendings self-clean after 90 min, caps of 5 pending per phone and max(courts*8, 24) per venue-day. Price computed server-side.

steps.title: Pending row counts against capacity
steps.detail: The request has no court yet — the slot is protected by the capacity check (bookings for that sport/hour vs court_count). The unique index (tenant, date, hour, court) guards the atomic court claim at confirm time.

steps.title: Staff review
steps.detail: The pending request surfaces in the staff console.

steps.title: Confirm
steps.detail: Staff JWT required. Court auto-claimed atomically via the <initial><n> claim loop — first free court wins.

steps.title: Counter-blocks enqueued
steps.detail: One durable job per other connected channel, written in the same transaction as the confirm.

steps.title: Scheduler tick
steps.detail: process_sync_jobs drains the queue holding the partner secrets — a 2am booking cannot double-sell a court.

steps.title: Jobs claimed with retry
steps.tech: 25/batch · FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED · backoff 30s×n · failed after 5
steps.detail: Failed pushes back off and retry; nothing outbound is fire-and-forget.

steps.title: Slot closed everywhere
steps.detail: The designed path. Today the DB processor records the block and logs to sync_log — the partner HTTP call is the scaffolded edge-function half.

flows.name: Staff walk-in booking
flows.summary: Manual entry by staff — it blocks the marketplaces exactly like an online booking, and leaves the provenance fingerprint that distinguishes humans from imports.

steps.title: Open bookings.html
steps.detail: Tenant-scoped session; lockdown requires real Supabase Auth, not a JS-compared PIN.

steps.title: Record
steps.detail: Server computes the rate and claims a court; source comes from the form (e.g. Walk-in).

steps.title: Confirmed row lands
steps.detail: The manual-entry fingerprint: fresh created_at, no ext_ref. (Channel imports set ext_ref; seed batches share one bulk created_at.)

steps.title: Channels blocked too
steps.detail: Same propagation as an online booking: record_booking calls propagate_block right after the insert — one durable sync_jobs row per other connected channel, so a walk-in can't be double-sold on Playo/Hudle/District.

steps.title: Worker pushes the blocks
steps.detail: These are the same jobs CourtSync's board monitors — a walk-in shows up there like any other block.

steps.title: Hour closed on marketplaces
steps.detail: The designed path: the court disappears from every channel within ~a minute of the front-desk entry (partner HTTP is the scaffolded half — today the processor records + logs each block).

steps.title: Visible on the CourtSync board
steps.detail: CourtSync reads the same sync_jobs queue, so the walk-in's blocks appear on the operator's channel board — and a stuck job can be re-driven from there.

steps.title: Telemetry
steps.detail: Outbox-backed insert into events — survives offline.

steps.title: Operator sees it
steps.detail: Shows in the 7-day per-academy feed with time and detail.

flows.name: Partner booking import
flows.summary: A booking sold on a marketplace flows in and closes the slot on every other channel.

steps.title: Webhook arrives
steps.detail: Playo/Hudle/District call in when a booking happens on their side (partner-poll is the pull fallback).

steps.title: Identity & credentials
steps.detail: The inbound call is authenticated by the venue's unique api_key — Vault plays no part in verifying webhooks; its partner credentials serve the outbound counter-block pushes.

steps.title: Booking ingested
steps.detail: Row inserted with ext_ref set — the imported-booking fingerprint — and source = channel name.

steps.title: Counter-blocks enqueued
steps.detail: Block jobs queued for every other connected channel.

steps.title: Queue drained
steps.detail: Next minute tick claims the jobs.

steps.title: Other channels blocked
steps.detail: The slot closes across the remaining marketplaces.

flows.name: Cancel / maintenance block
flows.summary: Rain, maintenance, or a change of plans — freeing a slot re-opens it everywhere, durably.

steps.title: Staff cancel or block
steps.detail: Cancel a booking (rain/maintenance reasons) or block a court range.

steps.title: Server does the change
steps.detail: Staff-guarded RPCs; refunds/credits stay a money question answered in Postgres.

steps.title: Slot freed
steps.detail: The partial unique index ignores cancelled rows — the hour is instantly sellable again.

steps.title: Unblock propagated
steps.detail: One durable unblock job per channel, same transactional pattern as blocking.

steps.title: Slot reopens everywhere
steps.detail: Marketplaces show the hour again — no manual channel juggling.

flows.name: Sync failure, retry & dead letters
flows.summary: What happens when a partner API is down — and how the operator finds out and recovers.

steps.title: Push fails
steps.detail: Partner API down or rejecting. The job records the error instead of vanishing (claimed in batches of 25, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED).

steps.title: Backoff scheduled
steps.detail: The job retires to the queue with a later next_run_at; the next tick retries it.

steps.title: Dead letter
steps.detail: The fifth failure stops retrying — the job parks as a dead letter instead of hammering the partner.

steps.title: Health surfaces it
steps.detail: Dead letters, stale integrations and queue age are first-class health fields.

steps.title: Operator alerted
steps.detail: Sidebar flips to Degraded; the Overview banner lists what to clear. Alerts only fire where CourtSync is actually sold (config.modules.booking).

steps.title: Recover
steps.detail: Operator inspects the venue's channel board, fixes the credential or triggers a re-sync; resolves inline from the activity feed.

flows.name: Resolving what a player owes
flows.summary: resolve_fee(): one SQL function, seven levels of override — the reason two screens can never quote different amounts.

steps.title: THE HOUSE RULE
steps.detail: The fee chain, renewal roll-forward and payout split are SQL functions called by web, Android AND the reminder engine. No client does the arithmetic.

steps.title: Walk the chain
steps.detail: 7-level precedence: enrolment override → member → batch → centre+sport → sport → centre → tenant default. First hit wins.

steps.title: Rules consulted
steps.detail: All tenant-scoped; the same rows serve every client.

steps.title: Same answer on Android
steps.detail: Verified in source: the phone calls the identical RPC — a parent's WhatsApp message and the manager's screen can never disagree.

flows.name: Recording a payment
flows.summary: record_fee_payment() is the ONE write path — it rolls the renewal forward, writes the timeline, and closes the reminder, atomically.

steps.title: Staff record a payment
steps.detail: Amount, mode (cash/UPI/card) against an enrollment.

steps.title: The one write path
steps.detail: Every fee payment goes through this function — there is no second door.

steps.title: Coverage computed
steps.detail: Which months this payment covers — partial and advance payments handled in SQL, not in a client.

steps.title: Renewal rolls forward
steps.detail: Next due date advances; the student profile gets an append-only timeline entry.

steps.title: Reminder closed
steps.detail: Any open reminder for this enrollment resolves — the parent stops getting chased the moment money lands.

steps.title: Metrics update
steps.detail: AM's numbers move on the next hydrate. void_payment()/confirm_payment() exist for reversals — also SQL.

flows.name: Renewal reminder ladder
flows.summary: WhatsApp-first dues chasing — one SQL function feeds both the cron auto-sender and the staff screen, so they always agree.

steps.title: Renewal approaches
steps.detail: The console shows who is coming due per centre.

steps.title: One function, two surfaces
steps.detail: Computes who is due and for how much. The cron uses it to send; the staff screen uses the SAME function for the manual click-to-send list.

steps.title: The ladder
steps.detail: Each stage is a state in reminder_events: queued → sent → delivered → read; failures → retry_scheduled.

steps.title: WhatsApp send
steps.detail: The parent gets a polite, correctly-priced message — the amount came from resolve_fee(), so it is never wrong.

steps.title: +15d: STOP
steps.detail: Automation stands down — past two weeks overdue, a human must call. No parent gets robo-chased forever.

steps.title: Timeline closes the loop
steps.detail: Reminder and eventual payment both append to the student profile.

flows.name: Centre revenue share
flows.summary: Raj coaches at venues he doesn't own — the payout split is computed in Postgres like every other money rule.

steps.title: The business shape
steps.detail: Schools, clubs and communities host the batches; a centre can take rent or a % of collections.

steps.title: Split computed
steps.detail: The month's collections divided per centre by its share rules — in SQL, per the house rule.

steps.title: Inputs
steps.detail: Same payment rows the fee chain wrote; no parallel bookkeeping.

steps.title: Payout statement
steps.detail: Raj sees what each centre is owed; the Android app shows identical numbers.

flows.name: Usage telemetry → activity feed
flows.summary: Every tenant-app action becomes a durable event; the operator reads them as a per-academy activity feed.

steps.title: Any page opens
steps.detail: cloud.js auto-logs page views and keeps a 12-crumb ring of recent actions; client_error events attach the crumbs for replay-free triage.

steps.title: Durable anon insert
steps.detail: tenant_id, name, props, session_id, page. Public INSERT is allowed by design (events_public_w); the offline outbox flushes when the connection returns.

steps.title: Row lands
steps.detail: Operator-only SELECT policy — telemetry flows from anyone, but only the operator reads it.

steps.title: Operator opens AM
steps.detail: Any academy card → detail view.

steps.title: Aggregates
steps.detail: usage_daily, sessions_30d, active_days, last_event_at, errors_30d — computed server-side per tenant.

steps.title: 7-day raw feed
steps.detail: Day-by-day actions with time and detail, page-view summaries per screen, session counts, idle days marked 'No activity'.

flows.name: Portfolio review & billing badge
flows.summary: Cross-tenant KPIs with PII minimization — and exactly how the paid/pending/overdue badge is derived.

steps.title: Open the console
steps.detail: Shell renders instantly, then hydrates.

steps.title: Operator sign-in
steps.detail: Password grant → JWT; tokens refresh transparently 90s before expiry.

steps.title: Three RPCs hydrate
steps.detail: Per-tenant KPIs; jobs/stale-feeds/dead-letters; data gaps.

steps.title: Aggregates only
steps.detail: Cross-tenant math runs server-side. Phone lists never leave a tenant — contacts_count crosses the boundary, contacts don't.

steps.title: Badge derivation
steps.tech: overdue: status='overdue' OR renews_on < today · paid: active|paid · else pending
steps.detail: Derived at render, not stored. 'Move to paid' = set_subscription(): sets status AND rolls a past renewal forward so the badge doesn't flip straight to overdue.

steps.title: Audited control
steps.detail: Every billing change writes an audit row; a tenant's own staff cannot mark themselves paid.

flows.name: Federated tenant reporting (Gen Alpha)
flows.summary: A tenant doesn't have to live in this database to appear in the console — Gen Alpha reports instead of migrating.

steps.title: Why federated
steps.detail: Gen Alpha predates the platform and is live with real families on its own 19-table Supabase. Migrating would risk live data for zero owner-visible benefit.

steps.title: Ops data stays home
steps.detail: Bookings, members, payments — all remain in Gen Alpha's backend.

steps.title: Telemetry reports in
steps.detail: Posted to the shared events table with the public anon key — no new secret, no new endpoint, no new table.

steps.title: Counts only
steps.detail: Rollups are forgeable by anyone holding the public key — acceptable for aggregate dashboard numbers, and exactly why nothing personal goes in one.

steps.title: Fallback aggregation
steps.detail: When a tenant's native rows are empty, the portfolio falls back to its latest rollup — the card shows real numbers.

steps.title: Billing optional
steps.detail: Gen Alpha runs its own infrastructure, so it's tracked but not billed.

flows.name: Hourly watchdog & anon probe
flows.summary: Three shape checks plus one behavior check — because the worst leak this platform had passed every shape check.

steps.title: Hourly tick
steps.detail: Runs the audit battery and logs anything suspicious.

steps.title: Shape checks
steps.detail: Anon-reachable policies without a tenant/auth predicate — including {public}-role policies, the pseudo-role blind spot that let two orphan app tables sit open while the audit read green (fixed 0033/0034); definer functions anon can execute (empty except the 4 public ones); policy-referenced functions anon can't run.

steps.title: Behavior check
steps.detail: Actually CALLS the dangerous endpoints as anon, hourly — plus a per-tenant sweep: every tenant's timetable scope checked both directions (private = anon sees nothing, publisher = anon sees exact live counts), and the closed orphan tables' read AND write paths. Asserts on CONTENT, never length.

steps.title: Canary
steps.detail: False when the events sink goes quiet despite recent traffic — catches silent telemetry death.

steps.title: Warnings logged
steps.detail: Anything failing lands in the platform log.

steps.title: Console surfaces it
steps.detail: AM's health score, system card, and needs-attention banner reflect the watchdog within the hour.

flows.name: Applying a migration
flows.summary: One ledger-checked runner, blast-radius awareness, and measurement before belief.

steps.title: Dry-run first, always
steps.detail: A change to a shared table reaches every live tenant, including apps in daily use. The dry run proves the SQL parses — not that the system still works.

steps.title: Ledger gate
steps.detail: The runner refuses a file already applied, and refuses louder if it changed since. Never rename an applied .sql file.

steps.title: Atomic apply
steps.detail: The migration and its ledger entry commit together or not at all.

steps.title: Exercise the real path
steps.tech: real anon key · before/after row counts
steps.detail: After touching any policy OR grant: call the endpoints as anon and compare against known-good values. Both past outages were caught by measuring, not by reading SQL.

steps.title: The lessons behind the rule
steps.detail: A policy predicate runs as the calling role — an anon-unreadable subquery silently denies every row. Revoking is_locked() from PUBLIC took Raj's timetable down; policy helpers are SECURITY DEFINER for a reason.

flows.name: Nightly snapshot & the backup gap
flows.summary: What the platform can recover from — and, honestly, what it can't yet.

steps.title: Nightly snapshot
steps.detail: Copies the tenant tables every night, keeps 14 days.

steps.title: Into the same database
steps.detail: Covers a migration doing more than intended — which has happened.

steps.title: The gap
steps.detail: If the project itself is lost, the snapshots go with it. There is no restorable daily backup today.

steps.title: The fix
steps.detail: Known, priced, and on the list — the honest line in the ops docs rather than a false sense of safety.
